title.en: Write the voltage, current and power gain of a CE amplifier

say.en: Put 10 millivolts into a CE amplifier and you may get 2 volts out, but upside down. Today we measure that gain and learn the decibel scale engineers use for it. In this lesson: Write the voltage, current and power gain of a CE amplifier.
Explain phase reversal.
Express gain in decibels.

body.en: For a CE amplifier the current gain is $A_i \approx \beta$ ($h_{fe}$) and the input resistance is $r_{in} \approx h_{ie}$. The voltage gain is $A_v = v_o/v_i = -\beta r_L / r_{in}$, where $r_L = R_C \parallel R_L$ is the AC load. The minus sign shows the 180° phase reversal: when the base current rises, the collector current rises, the drop across $R_C$ rises and the collector voltage falls. *Power gain* $A_p = |A_v| \times A_i$, which is why CE gives the highest power gain of the three configurations.

narration.en: Voltage gain is minus beta times the AC load over the input resistance. Power gain is voltage gain times current gain.
narration.kn: ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ವರ್ಧನೆ Av = −β rL/rin. ಋಣ ಚಿಹ್ನೆ 180° ಹಂತ ತಿರುವನ್ನು ಸೂಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಶಕ್ತಿ ವರ್ಧನೆ = ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ವರ್ಧನೆ × ಪ್ರವಾಹ ವರ್ಧನೆ.

say.en: Voltage gain is minus beta times the AC load over the input resistance. Power gain is voltage gain times current gain. Ai is approximately beta hfe.
say.kn: ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ವರ್ಧನೆ Av equals -beta rL over rin. ಋಣ ಚಿಹ್ನೆ 180 degrees ಹಂತ ತಿರುವನ್ನು ಸೂಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಶಕ್ತಿ ವರ್ಧನೆ = ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ವರ್ಧನೆ times ಪ್ರವಾಹ ವರ್ಧನೆ.

say.en: Av equals -beta rL over rin equals -hfe rL over hie.
Ap = |Av| times Ai.
CE gives the highest power gain.

narration.en: On the board: voltage gain and phase reversal.

say.en: Here are the input and output on the same time axis. The output is far bigger and is upside down.
The voltage gain is minus beta times the AC load, divided by the input resistance. The AC load is RC in parallel with RL.
Current gain is beta and power gain is the product of the two. Engineers quote these gains in decibels.

title.en: Gains of a CE amplifier, in decibels

narration.en: Current gain Ai ≈ hfe, voltage gain Av = −hfe rL/hie (the minus sign is the 180° phase reversal), power gain Ap = |Av| × Ai. In decibels: 20 log |Av| and 10 log Ap. Connecting a load RL = 4.7 kΩ lowers the AC load rL = RC ∥ RL and so the voltage gain.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಲಾಭ Ai ≈ hfe, ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ಲಾಭ Av = −hfe rL/hie, ಶಕ್ತಿ ಲಾಭ Ap = |Av| × Ai. ಡೆಸಿಬೆಲ್: 20 log |Av|, 10 log Ap. 4.7 kΩ ಭಾರ ಜೋಡಿಸಿದರೆ rL ಮತ್ತು ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ಲಾಭ ಕಡಿಮೆ.

say.en: Current gain Ai is approximately hfe, voltage gain Av equals -hfe rL over hie (the minus sign is the 180 degrees phase reversal), power gain Ap = |Av| times Ai. In decibels: 20 log |Av| and 10 log Ap. Connecting a load RL equals 4.7 k ohms lowers the AC load rL equals RC is parallel to RL and so the voltage gain.
say.kn: ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಲಾಭ Ai is approximately hfe, ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ಲಾಭ Av equals -hfe rL over hie, ಶಕ್ತಿ ಲಾಭ Ap = |Av| times Ai. ಡೆಸಿಬೆಲ್: 20 log |Av|, 10 log Ap. 4.7 k ohms ಭಾರ ಜೋಡಿಸಿದರೆ rL ಮತ್ತು ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ಲಾಭ ಕಡಿಮೆ.

body.en: The decibel is a logarithmic unit: *power gain* in dB $= 10\log_{10}(P_o/P_i)$ and voltage gain in dB $= 20\log_{10}(V_o/V_i)$. Logarithms turn the multiplication of stage gains into addition, compress very large numbers, and match the logarithmic response of the ear. A voltage gain of 10 is 20 dB, 100 is 40 dB, and a fall to 0.707 of the value is −3 dB.

narration.en: For power we use ten log, for voltage twenty log. A voltage gain of one hundred is forty decibels.
narration.kn: ಶಕ್ತಿ ವರ್ಧನೆ ಡೆಸಿಬೆಲ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ 10 log(Po/Pi), ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ವರ್ಧನೆ 20 log(Vo/Vi). ನೂರು ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ವರ್ಧನೆ ಎಂದರೆ 40 dB.

say.en: For power we use ten log, for voltage twenty log. A voltage gain of one hundred is forty decibels. Gp equals 10 log(Po over Pi) dB.
say.kn: ಶಕ್ತಿ ವರ್ಧನೆ ಡೆಸಿಬೆಲ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ 10 log(Po over Pi), ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ವರ್ಧನೆ 20 log(Vo over Vi). ನೂರು ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ವರ್ಧನೆ ಎಂದರೆ 40 dB.

say.en: Gv equals 20 log(Vo over Vi) dB.
Gain 10 gives 20 dB; 100 gives 40 dB; 1000 gives 60 dB.
0.707 times gives minus 3 dB.

problem.en: A CE amplifier has hfe = 100, hie = 1 kΩ, RC = 4 kΩ and RL = 4 kΩ. Find the voltage gain, its value in dB and the power gain.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A CE amplifier has hfe = 100, hie = 1 kΩ, RC = 4 kΩ and RL = 4 kΩ. Find the voltage gain, its value in dB and the power gain.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A CE amplifier has hfe equals 100, hie equals 1 k ohms, RC equals 4 k ohms and RL equals 4 k ohms. Find the voltage gain, its value in dB and the power gain.
rL equals RC is parallel to RL equals 4 times 4 over 8 equals 2 k ohms.
Av equals -hfe rL over hie equals minus 100 times 2 over 1 equals minus 200.
Gain in dB equals 20 log 200 equals 46.0 dB.
Ap = |Av| times Ai equals 200 times 100 equals 20 000 equals 43.0 dB.
So the answer is Av equals minus 200 46.0 dB; Ap equals 20 000 43.0 dB.

problem.en: An amplifier gives 2 W output for 40 mW input. Express its power gain in dB.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. An amplifier gives 2 W output for 40 mW input. Express its power gain in dB.

say.en: Let us work this out together. An amplifier gives 2 watts output for 40 mW input. Express its power gain in dB.
Ap equals 2 over 0.04 equals 50.
Gp equals 10 log 50 equals 17.0 dB.
So the answer is About 17 dB.

body.en: For voltage: double = +6 dB, ×10 = +20 dB, half = −6 dB. For power: double = +3 dB, ×10 = +10 dB. Break any gain into 2s and 10s and add.

narration.en: Decibel shortcuts. For voltage: double = +6 dB, ×10 = +20 dB, half = −6 dB. For power: double = +3 dB, ×10 = +10 dB. Break any gain into 2s and 10s and add.

say.en: Decibel shortcuts. For voltage: double = plus 6 dB, times 10 = plus 20 dB, half equals minus 6 dB. For power: double = plus 3 dB, times 10 = plus 10 dB. Break any gain into 2 seconds and 10 seconds and add.
